notes: Hand-picked for the classic 2 to 3 week Madagascar route: Antananarivo and the Tana rice fields, Andasibe-Mantadia, Ranomafana, Isalo and Ankarafantsika (areas.json). BirdNET GeoModel is nearly blind to the island's forest endemics (Helmet Vanga scores 0.02, Scaly Ground-Roller 0.04), so the model was used only to confirm the widespread and wetland birds; the forest, dry-forest and Isalo specialities are listed by hand from eBird's species lists per province and from what a visitor meets on that route. More than half are endemic. Left to the packs: the far north (Masoala, Marojejy, Montagne d'Ambre, Ankarana, Nosy Be), the dry west (Kirindy, Bemaraha, Mahajanga, Kinkony) and the spiny south-west (Ifaty, Zombitse, Tsimanampetsotsa, Berenty). Left out on purpose: sea birds of the open ocean, vagrants and rare migrants, Madagascar Pochard (a handful of birds in one lake), Madagascar Grebe, Meller's Duck, Slender-billed Flufftail, Tsingy Forest Rail, Bernier's Teal, Red-tailed Newtonia and Dusky Tetraka (almost never seen), introduced Mallard, House Sparrow, Rock Dove and Common Waxbill, and Squacco Heron (rare visitor, only a lookalike of the Malagasy Pond Heron). American Barn Owl is the database's row for the island's Barn Owl; it is not in the trip until that row is fixed. Species ranges are set from memory and eBird province lists: check them against a field guide. Left out for lack of usable photos: Henst's Goshawk, Nelicourvi Weaver, Forest Fody, Grey-crowned Tetraka, Green Jery, Brown Emutail and Grey Emutail.
